slides.title: Async Context Managers (`async with`)
slides.prompt: Asynchronous context managers enable non-blocking setup and cleanup operations in asyncio programs. They implement `__aenter__()` and `__aexit__()` which return awaitable coroutines and are consumed using `async with`.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio

class AsyncConnection:
    async def __aenter__(self):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1) # Simulate async connection setup
        return self

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1) # Simulate async cleanup

async def main():
    async with AsyncConnection() as conn:
        print('Connected asynchronously!')

slides.title: Invalid Usage Error
slides.prompt: What happens if you use standard `with` instead of `async with` on an asynchronous context manager?
options: A AttributeError or TypeError is raised indicating missing `__enter__` method
It automatically upgrades execution to an async event loop
It triggers an immediate system warning and returns None
slides.correctAnswer: A AttributeError or TypeError is raised indicating missing `__enter__` method
